optimization.action_description: Add a CUDA routing_method_type=1 packer that emits TRT-LLM PackedScoreIdx<bf16> as int32 [T, top_k], with low 16 bits holding the bf16 routing weight and high 16 bits holding the expert id.
optimization.expected_impact: Provide the routing/permutation input contract needed by a custom TRT-LLM-style Blackwell FP4 grouped GEMM path, avoiding ambiguity in the packed precomputed-routing format.
optimization.risks_and_rollback: This binding is not used by the default scalar candidate path. Roll back this memory entry and the routing_pack_type1 binding if the next grouped-GEMM implementation chooses a different routing metadata contract.

evidence: routing_pack_type1 bitwise matched a Python reproduction of the CUDA insertion-sort TopK and PackedScoreIdx<bf16> packing for both bf16 and fp32 logits.
CUDA routing_pack_type1 output fed into flashinfer.trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe exactly matched flashinfer.trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe for G11 tokens=8: max_abs=0.0, max_rel=0.0.
Full G11 CUDA-packed routed FlashInfer probe exactly matched full FlashInfer in the same process: max_abs=0.0, max_rel=0.0.
Default candidate G11 tokens=8 correctness still passes after adding the binding: max_abs=0.00390625, max_rel=1.3259259462356567.

performance.note: The FlashInfer routed backend measurements are decomposition probes only and are not candidate performance. They show that full-G11 routing is not the dominant gap; the custom implementation still needs Blackwell FP4 tensor-core grouped GEMM/finalize.

source_findings.packed_score_idx_layout: flashinfer/data/include/flashinfer/trtllm/fused_moe/RoutingKernel.h defines PackedScoreIdx<DataType> as { DataType score; int16_t idx; }, so int32 storage is low16=bf16 score and high16=expert id.
source_findings.flashinfer_routed_api: flashinfer.fused_moe.core.trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe accepts precomputed packed topk ids and routes them through the same TRT-LLM FP4 MoE backend.

quality_gate.failure_reason: The packed routing contract is now implemented and verified, but the default candidate is still scalar stage1/stage2 and remains far slower than FlashInfer on the full TP1 G11 target.

next_step.description: Use routing_pack_type1 metadata to drive a custom SM103 NVFP4 grouped GEMM stage that consumes FlashInfer prepared weights/scales and replaces the scalar stage1/stage2 kernels.
